prerequisites: Solid foundations in: Mathematical Analysis I and II: differential and integral calculus, ordinary differential equations, vector algebra, differential operators (gradient, divergence, curl) and divergence and curl theorems.
General Physics I (Mechanics): kinematics and dynamics of point and rigid body, concepts of force, moment, work and energy.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the principles of conservation of mass, momentum, and energy in both integral (macroscopic) and differential (microscopic) forms.
Solve engineering problems related to the calculation of hydrostatic thrusts, head losses in industrial hydraulic circuits, and aerodynamic forces on submerged bodies.
Use dimensional analysis for the design and interpretation of experimental tests on scale models.
Understand elementary thermofluidodynamic phenomena related to compressible flows in nozzles and choked flows.

syllabus_topics: Introduction, basic concepts, fluid properties
Fluid statics
Fluid kinematics: Eulerian and Lagrangian description
Elementary equations of fluid dynamics - conservation of mass and energy (Bernoulli)
Integral formulation of conservation equations
Differential equations of fluid motion
Dimensional analysis and similitude
Internal viscous flows: flows in conduits
External viscous flows: flow around bodies, drag and lift, boundary layer
Approximate solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation
Laminar and turbulent flows
Compressible flows
Introduction and Fluid Properties: Adhesion condition. Vapor pressure and cavitation. Viscosity and Newtonian fluids. Surface tension. Calculation of shear stresses in viscometers and fluid gaps.

Fluid Statics: Hydrostatic pressure and manometers. Hydrostatic forces on submerged flat and curved surfaces. Archimedes' thrust, buoyancy and stability. Calculation of forces and moments on bulkheads and dams.

Fluid Kinematics: Lagrangian and Eulerian description. Streamlines, streaklines, and pathlines. Vorticity, rotationality, and strain-rate tensor. Reynolds Transport Theorem (RTT). Analytical determination of streamlines and material acceleration.

Bernoulli Equation and Integral Energy Formulation: Bernoulli equation: derivation, hypotheses and limitations. Piezometric and total head lines. General energy equation for open systems, alpha factor and head losses. Energy balances in hydraulic systems and Venturi meters.

Integral Momentum Formulation: Conservation of mass and linear/angular momentum for fixed and moving control volumes. Beta correction factor. Calculation of anchoring forces on flanged bends, nozzles and jets on blades.

Dimensional Analysis and Similitude: Buckingham's Pi theorem and method of repeating variables. Dimensionless groups (Reynolds, Froude, Mach). Similitude and scale models. Integrated exercise: Calculation of dimensionless groups and operating conditions for scale models.

Differential Equations of Fluid Motion: Differential continuity equation. Stream function. Derivation and physical meaning of the terms of the Navier-Stokes equations for incompressible fluids. Verification of permissible velocity fields and calculation of pressure gradients.

Approximate Solutions of the Navier-Stokes Equations: Exact solutions for steady parallel flows (Couette and Poiseuille). Euler equations for inviscid flows. Irrotational flows and velocity potential. Analytical derivation of velocity profiles and flow rates between plates and conduits.

Internal Viscous Flows: Laminar and turbulent regime in conduits. Entrance region and fully developed flow. Distributed (Darcy-Weisbach, Moody chart, Colebrook) and concentrated head losses. Energy balance and hydraulic design of an industrial circuit.

External Viscous Flows and Boundary Layer: Prandtl's boundary layer theory. Laminar (Blasius) and turbulent boundary layer on a flat plate. Characteristic thicknesses (nominal, displacement, momentum). Calculation of thicknesses and global shear stress on a flat plate.

Flow around Bodies: Drag and Lift: Drag forces (friction and form drag) and lift forces. Boundary layer separation phenomenon. C_D and C_L coefficients for cylinders, spheres and airfoils. Calculation of aerodynamic drag and lift forces.

Compressible Flows: Speed of sound and Mach number. Stagnation properties and state. Isentropic flows in convergent and de Laval nozzles. Choked flow. Introduction to normal shock waves. Calculation of thermodynamic properties in de Laval nozzles.
assessment_rules: The assessment of acquired skills takes place through an exam divided into two phases: a Written Test and an Oral Test. Passing the written test with a grade of at least 18/30 is binding for access to the oral exam. The oral exam verifies critical learning of the subject, physical understanding of phenomena, and rigor in presenting fundamental mathematical derivations.
